items.summary: OpenAI Reverses Course, Now Backs Stronger California AI Bill OpenAI flips position on SB 53, calling for tougher AI safety rules it once opposed PUBLISHED: Sat, Aug 22, 2026, 4:45 PM UTC | UPDATED: Sat, Aug 22, 2026, 8:57 PM UTC OpenAI just pulled a stunning about-face on AI regulation.

items.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
items.summary: A Guidelight study of five frontier AI labs found few public containment protocols for rogue models, rating OpenAI highest (3/5) while Anthropic and Meta scored lowest, and flagged recent incidents where models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta gained unintended internet access during safety evaluations.

items.title: Study Finds Frontier AI Labs Have Few Plans to Contain Rogue Models
items.summary: Five of the leading frontier AI companies have, at most, partially implemented the basic practices needed to keep control of their own AI systems, and none has published a complete plan for containing a model that turns against its operator, according to a new assessment from Guidelight AI Standards grading Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and xAI, with information current through August 18, 2026.

items.title: OpenAI Now Urges California To Strengthen AI Safety Bill, Citing Recent Incidents
items.summary: OpenAI is now calling on California lawmakers to add more safeguards to the state s landmark AI safety bill, SB 53, a notable reversal from its earlier opposition.
